Here, the denominator is the imaginary number $8\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+8\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-8\text{i},$ or simply $-8\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-8\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-9+7\text{i}}{8\text{i}} & =\frac{-9+7\text{i}}{8\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-8\text{i}}{-8\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{72\text{i}-56{\text{i}}^{2}}{-64{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{72\text{i}-56(-1)}{-64(-1)} \\  & =\frac{56+72\text{i}}{64}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{56+72\text{i}}{64} & =\frac{56}{64}+\frac{72}{64}\text{i} \\  & =(\frac{7}{8})+(\frac{9}{8})\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
